title: Scrolling the timeline along time keeps every frame at full speed
goal: When the timeline scrolls along time quickly (held at an edge while dragging, or dragged by its scroller), about one frame in twenty is late, because every step redraws the whole editor window rather than just the timeline. Scrolling should hold sixty frames a second without a hitch.
notes: Measured 2026-10-11 by the runner on a-selection-box-on-the-timeline-scrolls-the-time. Command: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/box-scrolls-at-the-edge-walk.json. Its boxToEdge log line, after the edge ticker was capped at 60 Hz: right edge at full speed across the 14 s sample opened to 3.5 s across: 100 frames, ms between them p50 16.7 p95 33.3 max 39.2; left edge: p50 16.7 p95 33.9 max 39.3; the 5 s hold opened right in: p50/p95/max 16.7. At 120 Hz before the cap it was p50 17-20 ms, p95 about 26 ms. A sample of the probe during a 12 s hold: of 1407 main-thread samples about 1150 are NSHostingView.layout > ViewGraphRootValueUpdater.render under CA::Transaction commit (the whole window re-laid out per timelineZoom change); TimelineTrackRow.body about 46, ClipPiecesBar.body about 12, EditorState.motionStripCycleMS about 31; the display-link ticker itself about 3. The walk harness timer watchForWindowsOverThePerson took 111 samples (8 percent), so walk numbers overstate the app cost somewhat. Likely lever: views outside the timeline that read timelineWindow or motionStripRuler (or documentMomentChanged side effects), so a pan invalidates the whole window; panTimeline from the overview scroller shares the path.
acceptance: box-scrolls-at-the-edge-walk, held at the right edge across the sample recording, reports p95 between frames at or under 17.5 ms
A time profile of that hold shows the per-step work confined to the timeline (ruler, lanes, clip bars), not a full window layout
The 5 second hold at the end of the same walk stays at p50, p95 and max of 16.7 ms

log.note: Reproduced: right edge p95 33.3/38.4 ms twice. Profile: the 'whole window layout' was SwiftUI's normal NSHostingView pass; the bodies run were all timeline (track rows incl. headers, dock grid via the lane box gesture reading the ruler in body, every clip bar). Clip bars were ~40% (hiding them: 1542 -> 921 ms busy). Fixed by drawing bars from their own start and sliding them (0c297537).

left rough: the walk harness's window watcher (watchForWindowsOverThePerson, CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo at 50 Hz) takes 7-10% of the main thread in every walk; walk-only, so not filed. A 40-60 ms single frame shows when the box picks a new clip mid-scroll (selection change rebuilds the panel); not in acceptance, logged only. The sound tag at a clip's start sits up to 60 pt off the lane's left edge (shows '...sic'), same as before this change.

Clip bars drawn from their own start and slid along (SlidAlongTheTimeline), cut to a stretch that moves every half window (TimelineDrawnStretch); lanes, labels and pinned names redraw on their own (DrawnOnItsOwn); zoom stored as scale + start. box-scrolls-at-the-edge-walk x3 at Next defaults: right edge p95 33.3 -> 16.7 ms, left 16.7, 5 s hold p50/p95/max 16.7; clip bar bodies per hold 428 -> 24, track rows and dock grid 0 (body counts now in the walk's log line; sample shows only timeline bodies per step). 33 related walks green, Scripts/test.sh green (13135 tests). Commit 0c297537.
